pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:396 The published input schema is a hand-written JSON literal while the enforced contract is a separate set of serde structs in table-app (items is an unbounded Vec there), and the only binding test checks key names, so the two authorities for one contract can drift apart without any gate failing.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:396 Published schema and validator (agent_request.rs:53 Vec<PurchaseLine>) are two hand-kept artifacts; server.rs:1164 checks only that keys are advertised. Also: a params object that fails the Call envelope is answered in-band as MalformedCall (lib.rs:544), not as a protocol error. Annotations carry no idempotentHint, and read-only hints are asserted against the declaration (server.rs:1203) but never probed against a recording stand-in.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:402 The listing publishes only the addressable name, with no rename-stable identifier, even though refusals and outcomes are persisted per tool in the audit trail.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:237 A single-machine server bound to a loopback port, where the decision table calls for standard streams. Mitigated: Host allowlist, refusal of any Origin, a shared secret and a per-session bearer token (lib.rs:454-472).

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:460 Constant-time secret check plus a per-session token that is role-scoped, expires in 120 s and can be revoked. Listing is deliberately token-gated, and a pending grant can list but not invoke (lib.rs:169).
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:297 One Tool enum is the registry, there is one handle() door, and the door enforces the deadline (:554) and the result-size cap (:592) uniformly.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:573 One 30 s budget per call. On timeout the result is an error that reports the outcome as unknown and names a different recovery probe (table_view), never an empty success. Elapsed and budget figures are not reported.
crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:67 Model output can only add caution over the deterministic rules. server.rs:653 asserts that counterparty NOTE text never reaches the agent through table_view.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:286 The agent surface is a strict subset by subtraction: no role catalog carries a money tool, and the owner-only accept is refused with a code that names the owner.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:173 Deal and run are bound to the grant by the host, not supplied as an ambient-selection argument.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:311 Seven tools in total and at most five per role, so no host tool budget is under pressure.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:102 A single in-process loopback server with no replicas, so there is no affinity routing.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:359 No request pauses for a person; propose_purchase returns a pending status immediately, and there is no elicitation.

pairs.registryProposal: transport-selection's table assumes the host can spawn the server. Here the server lives inside the wallet process and the engine (an MCP client) is a separate CLI child, so standard streams would need a relay shim. The table should say whether a loopback listener with Host allowlist, Origin refusal, a per-process secret and a per-run token is an accepted form or still the local-port trap.
